To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein-folding thermodynamic landscape is not a simple two-dimensional funnel, but a complex multi-dimensional landscape, with many metastable states, that is accessible to experimental investigation by using perturbation methods.
The free energies and the rate constants for folding and unfolding of proteins are related by the principle of detailed balance.
the folding thermodynamics of the 10-residue protein GB1 can be described by a simple two-state transition between the unfolded and the folded states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamic properties of biomolecules, in particular proteins.
the development and application of new experimental methods to study biomolecular structure, dynamics, thermodynamics and function.
the development of new experimental methods and their application in the study of protein-folding kinetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the folding kinetics of the proteins is determined by the free-energy landscape of the proteins.
the free-energy landscapes of proteins can be studied in detail with the help of kinetic experiments, but that this approach has to be combined with other experimental and theoretical methods.
, in general, it is difficult to determine the free-energy landscape of a protein from a single experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method, which allows us to measure the kinetics and the thermodynamics of protein folding and unfolding in parallel.
the free-energy landscape is a function of both time and temperature.
we have been able to measure the free energies of folding and unfolding of several proteins and peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now determine free energy landscapes of biomolecules by perturbing and then watching them return to equilibrium.
the relaxation dynamics of proteins is a very useful and powerful tool to determine protein-folding thermodynamic parameters.
the folding kinetics of proteins can be used to determine the thermodynamics of folding.
